subject: Erasure pathway, retention windows & residency — qualification follow-up
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finserve-analytics.com>, Rajesh Iyer <rajesh@finserve-analytics.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Erasure pathway, retention windows & residency — qualification follow-up

Hi Olivia / Rajesh —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps and a short qualification list so my solutions team can size the Dedicated/private options correctly.

Key points I captured from the call:
- You want a full account-level Right to Be Forgotten (RTBF) workflow for end users and admins, triggered via API or support ticket.
- Scope includes PII fields in text inputs and embeddings, plus model-generated artifacts tied to PII.
- Preferred residency: US (multi-region failover acceptable but primary data residency must remain in us-central-1).
- Retention targets: 30-day hot retention for active records, 365-day cold retention for audit logs, with an SLA for customer-requested deletes in 7–30 days depending on backup windows.
- Backup constraints: nightly snapshots to object store are on a 7-day retention cycle; you need confirmation on when backups are truncated after an RTBF event.

Open qualification questions for your team (please reply inline):
1) What formats do your delete requests come in today? (API, signed PDF, ticketing system)
2) Do you require deletion proof (signed attestation) or an audit log entry with hashed identifiers?
3) Which backup provider do you use (S3, GCS, other) and are snapshots encrypted with KMS you control?
4) Any regulatory mandates beyond GDPR/CCPA (e.g., FINRA, HIPAA) that affect retention policies?

Next steps we propose:
- I’ll share a concise erasure playbook (attached) that maps the API steps, backup retention impact, and expected purge timeline.
- Naomi can run a brief tech qualification to confirm KMS/backup compatibility and propose a fallback model for in-flight KV cache deletion.
- Ben will prepare a high-level Dedicated capacity estimate and cost delta for encrypted backups in your region.

Attachments: redwood-erasure-playbook-v1.pdf (summary), sample-delete-request-form.docx

If that looks right, can you confirm answers to the four questions above by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks —
Dev

--
Dev Patel

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Erasure pathway, retention windows & residency — qualification follow-up

Dev —

Thanks for the summary, that aligns well. Answers inline:
1) Delete requests today: primarily support tickets (Zendesk) and an internal portal that exports a CSV. We can add an API-based request but need a signed ticket fallback.
2) We require deletion proof for audit — a signed attestation for enterprise customers and an audit log entry (hashed IDs are fine) for self-service deletes.
3) Backups: we use AWS S3 with a lifecycle policy; snapshots are encrypted with our KMS (we control keys).
4) Regulation: not HIPAA, but we have FINRA-like recordkeeping requirements for certain product lines (audit retention 7 years) — need to map exemptions.

On backups: our internal compliance says we cannot permanently remove historical audit logs older than 7 years for certain records; can you confirm how Redwood treats immutable audit trails vs user-facing content?

We’d like the API path plus a ticketing fallback. Also, what is your typical purge timeline for objects in snapshots? You mentioned 7–30 days depending on backup window — can you specify conditions that push it to 30 days?

Olivia
Head of Platform Security, FinServe Analytics
olivia@finserve-analytics.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finserve-analytics.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Erasure pathway, retention windows & residency — qualification follow-up

Olivia —

Quick technical clarification from infra side:
- For object-store backups (S3) we have a two-phase purge for RTBF: 1) mark and logical-delete within primary store immediately; 2) queued snapshot tombstones applied at next snapshot compaction. Compaction frequency typically equals your snapshot cycle — for nightly snapshots, worst-case a record can stay in a snapshot for up to the snapshot retention window (we purge snapshots older than retention).
- If you control KMS keys and require key rotation or key destruction as proof of erasure, we can support a customer-managed KMS integration, but note that key destruction is irreversible and impacts restore for all tenants using that key.
- For audit logs: we provide immutable append-only audit logs with retention controls; we can mark user-identifiable content as pseudonymized for retention-exempt audit trails.

Attachment: sample-delete-request-form.docx (filled template for your team to try)

I’ll follow up with a short tech note that outlines the exact conditions that can extend purge to 30 days (long-running restores, cross-region snapshot replication, legal holds).

—Naomi
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Thanks all —

This is helpful. A couple of asks before we move toward a pilot:
- Can you provide a short matrix that maps: event (user delete request) -> immediate visible state (deleted from UI) -> status in backups -> expected final purge time and proof artifact?
- Please flag any cases where FINRA-style recordkeeping forces us to keep an immutable audit copy and how Redwood would support that (e.g., pseudonymization, export-only retention).

If you can get the matrix and the tech note by end of week, we can schedule a pilot kickoff with our security team next Tuesday.

Rajesh
